## Regressions

💭 nit  The copied test harness grew back in four small places the cleanup added or left
- key: src/window.test.setup.ts#copied-harness-regrowth
- where: `const HIDDEN = { includeHiddenElements: true }` in 5 files (round 1: 3): shell/ProjectHeader.test.native.tsx:11, Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:35, Sidebar.test.native.tsx:18, Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx:14, TopBar.test.native.tsx:14. The "testIDs inside a node" listing in 4 files: Sidebar.test.native.tsx:21-24, Shell.test.native.tsx:175-177, Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:74-76, ProjectHeader.test.native.tsx:135-137. core/api/project.test.ts:5-16 and :44-53, a file the cleanup created, re-implement clone, broken, rejected and cases from core/api/overview.test.helper.ts:6-23 and overview.test.ts:186-199, for the header schema. The screen copy SCREEN is declared twice: shell/StateView.test.native.tsx:26-29 and shell/model.problem.test.ts:9-12.
- why: CONTRIBUTING.md:88 says to use the shared builders, and each copy is one more place where a fix must be repeated: broken()'s per-path dedupe (overview.test.helper.ts:15-22) now lives in two files, and a fix to one leaves the other reporting duplicate paths.
- fix: add src/query.test.helper.ts exporting HIDDEN and `testIDsIn(node)`; add `brokenBy(schema, fixture)` to a src/core/api/schema.test.helper.ts and use it in overview.test.helper.ts and project.test.ts; declare SCREEN once in shell/model.test.helper.ts.
- approach-changing: no, it moves helpers.

## New findings

🟡 major  The restated-literal gate matches whole strings only, so a fixture id inside a path or testID, and copy inside a filled sentence, pass gate:lint
- key: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js#exact-match-only
- where: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js:95 (`table.get(value)`, an equality lookup) and :106-111 (string literals and expression-free templates only); CONTRIBUTING.md:57-60 documents "equals". This rule holds the round-1 keys src/mocks/fixtures#retyped-fixture-values and src/shell/strings#retyped-copy-in-tests.
- why: in a test, an id usually sits inside a path or a testID, and copy inside a filled sentence; neither equals a protected value. Probe (ESLint on 11 planted lines, --stdin-filename src/shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx): 5 reported ('Northwind Furniture Co.' plain and as a template, 'Open menu', the inner literal of `tree-${'meridian-cgi-campaign'}`, 'Nadia R.'); 6 not reported ('tree-meridian-cgi-campaign', 'My focus 9', /Northwind Furniture Co\./, 'Nadia ' + 'R.', 'Northwind' with exact false, '3'). Today no test uses the embedded shape (grep of src, e2e and scripts: 0 hits; the same grep on the probe file: 1 hit), so the gap is in the gate, not in the code.
- fix: also report a string or expression-free template that contains (1) an id from src/mocks/fixtures/ids.ts as a whole token, matched by `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])<id>(?![A-Za-z0-9])`, and (2) outside model tests, a protected value of two or more words. RuleTester cases: '/w/creative-studio/registry', 'tree-meridian-cgi-campaign' and 'My focus 9' reported; 'creative-studios' and a test title holding 'Open menu' not. CONTRIBUTING.md:57 then says "equals or contains".
- approach-changing: no, it widens one rule.
- trigger: a plan C test writes `expect(screen.queryByTestId('tree-meridian-cgi-campaign')).toBeNull()`, while its positive twins read `tree-${IDS.meridian}`, and gate:lint passes. When IDS.meridian is renamed at src/mocks/fixtures/ids.ts:5, the twins follow the rename; the absence check now looks for an id that nothing draws, and passes whatever renders.
- guard-bypass: the rule compares whole values (no-restated-literals.js:95), so a value embedded in a longer string never matches; coverage and mutation judge production files only.
- design: yes, a containment match for fixture ids and multi-word values in local/no-restated-literals

💭 nit  Three absence checks are keyed on a hand-typed testID whose only positive query is in another file
- key: src/shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx#cross-file-absence-twin
- where: shell/Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:178-180 and :197 ('topbar-help'; the only positive query is shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:86); shell/Shell.test.native.tsx:131 ('workspace-switcher'; positive queries only in Sidebar.test.native.tsx, Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx and workspace.test.native.tsx). Probe (a script over the 47 in-scope test files): 11 testID-keyed absence checks have no positive query on the same id in the same test; for these 3, none exists in the same file.
- why: the checks meet CONTRIBUTING.md:128-134 literally (the same literal as the twin), but the twin is in another file. Rename 'topbar-help' in TopBar.tsx and fix the red TopBar.test.native.tsx:86: the phone check (:178-180) and the web-tablet check (:197) then pass even when Help draws there. TestIDs have no row in the source-of-truth table (CONTRIBUTING.md:47-53), so no rule links the copies.
- fix: give each check a positive twin in its own file: in the test at Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:241-257, after `setWidth(DESKTOP)`, add `expect(within(screen.getByTestId('topbar')).getByTestId('topbar-help')).toBeOnTheScreen()`; in Shell.test.native.tsx:48-56, add `expect(within(sidebar).getByTestId('workspace-switcher')).toBeOnTheScreen()`.
- approach-changing: no, two lines.

💭 nit  Shell tests assert the resolved design-system style instead of the tone and weight the shell passes
- key: src/shell#design-system-styles-in-shell-tests
- where: 18 assertions in 5 files on what Text, Glyph and CountBadge draw: shell/TopBar.test.native.tsx:40, :51 (fontWeight '600': the weight TopBar.tsx:38 passes, resolved by src/design-system/Text.styles.ts); Sidebar.test.native.tsx:113-119, :130, :132, :137-140; Sidebar.tree.test.native.tsx:46, :47, :51, :56, :58; ProjectHeader.test.native.tsx:78, :115, :119; Shell.narrow.test.native.tsx:93, :97, :116. Only StateView.test.native.tsx:14-23 uses the pass-through spy.
- why: CONTRIBUTING.md:84-87 and :107-108 say that a shell test proves what the shell passes and does not re-assert a design-system style. These assertions check the design system's tone and weight tables, so a design-system change (another token for tone muted) turns shell tests red while the shell is unchanged.
- fix: spy Text, Glyph and CountBadge as StateView.test.native.tsx:14-17 does, and assert the props, for example `expect(looksOf(names.at(-1)!)).toEqual([{ variant: 'crumb', tone: 'text', weight: '600' }])` (src/spy.test.helper.ts:11-14) at TopBar.test.native.tsx:40, and the tone of the active and plain rows; keep the styles the shell owns (the active row fill, the tab underline from ProjectHeader.styles.ts:51).
- approach-changing: no, local rewrites.

💭 nit  The Android fallback test cannot tell "falls back to the default" from "keeps the current language"
- key: src/shell/TopBar.test.android.tsx#fallback-equals-current
- where: shell/TopBar.test.android.tsx:7-15; the mount uses topBarModel(), whose language is English (TopBar.test.helper.tsx:17, model.test.helper.ts:40), and DEFAULT_LOCALE is English too (core/i18n/locale.test.ts:14-18).
- why: in-sample: the expected fallback equals the language already shown, so a TopBar that answered an unknown picker value with `model.language.value` instead of resolveLocale (TopBar.tsx:115) still passes "falls back to the default language".
- fix: `await mount({ onLocale, model: topBarModel(creativeStudio, { locale: 'vi', strings: STRINGS.vi }) })`, keeping `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(DEFAULT_LOCALE)`.
- approach-changing: no, one line.
